glosses: Tanning liquor, an aqueous extract of vegetable matter (tanbark, sumac, etc.) in a tanning vat used to tan leather.
An oozing, gentle flowing, or seepage, as of water through sand or earth.
Secretion, humour.
Juice, sap.
To be secreted or slowly leak.

examples.text: I promised him I would keep silence, but the story gradually oozed out, and the Cronsons left the country.
Pale slime oozed through all the surfaces; some of it dripped from the ceiling and burned Dennis as badly as the blazing sparks had done a moment before.
He was hard to understand because he spoke softly, and his Vermont accent was as thick as maple syrup oozing down a pile of pancakes.
Her heart constricted when she saw thick blood oozing from a wide gash in his forehead.

glosses: To give off a strong sense of (something); to exude.

examples.text: […] this room, where misfortune seems to ooze, where speculation lurks in corners, and of which Madame Vauquer inhales the warm, fetid air without being nauseated.
"Good servants are so hard to find," Chesna said, oozing arrogance.
There are no two ways about it: a Berardi dress oozes sex appeal from its very seams.

Newcastle had failed to penetrate a typically organised Stoke backline in the opening stages but, once Cabaye and then Cisse breached their defence, Newcastle oozed confidence and controlled the game with a swagger expected of a top-four team.

glosses: Soft mud, slime, or shells especially in the bed of a river or estuary.

examples.text: my son i' th' ooze is bedded.

It was May before the skunk cabbage began to push up through the ooze of the swamps, before the rhubarb reddened to the back corner of the garden and the spring peepers finally emerged and began abrading the edges of the night with their lovesick vibrato.

glosses: A pelagic marine sediment containing a significant amount of the microscopic remains of either calcareous or siliceous planktonic debris organisms.

examples.text: Seaweed were left on the blackened marble, while the salt ooze defaced the matchless works of art.

glosses: A piece of soft, wet, pliable ground.

glosses: Sortir, s’écouler presque imperceptiblement, en parlant d’un liquide, d’une humeur.

examples.text: […], on descendit dans des caves, on suivit des souterrains dont les parois,[…], laissaient suinter l’eau qui retombait en gouttes.
Les murs rongés de salpêtre laissent suinter les eaux montant de la terre et s’écaillent par larges plaques verdâtres.
Lui qui transpire si peu de manière générale, est en eau. La sueur suinte de son front, lui pique les yeux.
Sorda avait posé un cataplasme chaud de kaolin sur la poitrine du vieil homme pour tenter d’endiguer le flot d’écume qui suintait aux commissures de ses lèvres.
Ils voudraient que la société ressemble à un gros Justinland, un royaume pastel peuplé de licornes gentilles qui suintent des étoiles quand on les flatte.

glosses: Être le lieu d’où sort, s’écoule presque imperceptiblement un liquide, une humeur.

examples.text: Cette plaie est fermée, mais elle suinte encore.
Cette muraille suinte.

glosses: Suer, transpirer.

examples.text: La caissière, qui était très grosse et qui devait suinter depuis sa première enfance, lisait les horoscopes dans Jours de France.

glosses: Laisser échapper, faire transparaître un sentiment, une émotion.

examples.text: Vous voyez pas que cette personne suinte la haine ? Il suinte la haine je vous dis !
Malgré toutes les précautions, le secret a suinté.
Fraternel et affectueux lorsqu'il est avec le président de la République, Macron ne cesse en dehors de laisser suinter le mépris que lui inspire l'hôte de l'Élysée.

glosses: A crack, crevice, fissure, or hole which admits water or other fluid, or lets it escape.

examples.text: a leak in a roof
a leak in a boat
a leak in a gas pipe

glosses: The entrance or escape of a fluid through a crack, fissure, or other aperture.

examples.text: The leak gained on the ship's pumps.
The babies' diapers had big leaks.

glosses: A divulgation, or disclosure, of information previously held secret.

examples.text: The leaks by Chelsea Manning showed the secrets of the US military.

glosses: The person through whom such divulgation, or disclosure, occurs.

examples.text: […] so even if he was the leak, we would never know.
I was the leak. That the government didn't like our advice, and so I decided to leak it to 'bounce' them into having to follow it.
If he was the leak, it wasn't intentional. The same went for her mom, not that Cat thought her mom had any friends with top-level security clearance.

glosses: A loss of electricity through imperfect insulation, or the point where it occurs.
The gradual loss of a system resource caused by failure to deallocate previously reserved portions.

examples.text: resource leak
memory leak

glosses: An act of urination.

examples.text: I have to take a leak.

glosses: To allow fluid or gas to pass through an opening that should be sealed.

examples.text: The wells are believed to have been leaking oil for decades, long after the operating company ceased to exist.

glosses: (of a fluid or gas) To pass through an opening that should be sealed.

examples.text: The faucet has been leaking since last month.
No one realized that propane gas was leaking from a rusty tank in the concession area, slowly filling the unventilated room.

glosses: To disclose secret information surreptitiously or anonymously.

examples.text: Someone must have leaked it to our competitors that the new product will be out soon.
That's another of those irregular verbs, isn't it? I give confidential press briefings; you leak; he's being charged under section 2(A) of the Official Secrets Act.

glosses: To pass through when it would normally or preferably be blocked.

examples.text: A target that is not detected would not be intercepted and thus would leak through the single defensive layer.

glosses: To allow anything through that would normally or preferably be blocked.

examples.text: England were leaking penalties as Scotland played with pace and variety. Russell was starting to find his range and when he threaded through a grubber to Sean Maitland the winger did well to gather and keep the ball in play. Unfortunately, his pass inside just eluded Russell.

glosses: To urinate.

examples.text: I had to leak in the woods since there were no toilets around.
Why, you will allow vs ne're a Iourden, and then we leake in your Chimney: and your Chamber-lye breeds Fleas like a Loach.

Occasionally bums passed, Mexican mothers passed with children, and the prowl car came by and the cop got out to leak, but most of the time we were alone and mixing up our souls ever more and ever more till it would be terribly hard to say good-by.
Go and find a tree. I just leak against a^([sic]) oak over there.

glosses: To bleed.

examples.text: He shanked him, now he's leaking.

glosses: Leaky.

examples.text: Yet is the bottle leake, and bag so torne, / That all which I put in fals out anon […].
